themes_detail.label: Street Sign Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints spiked to 16 this week, up 574% from a 2.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.18), suggesting either concentrated vandalism, traffic accidents, or neglected maintenance creating safety hazards across CD 404.
evidence: 16 street sign damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 11.18 indicates statistically rare event
DOB records show 272 total permit filings in last 90 days, including 6 full demolitions, suggesting active construction that may correlate with infrastructure damage
reporting_angles: Are recent construction projects or demolitions damaging street signage? Cross-reference DOB permits with 311 complaint locations.
Interview DOT and precinct about enforcement and repair timelines for damaged signs that impair traffic flow and wayfinding.

themes_detail.label: Construction Lead Dust Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Construction lead dust complaints jumped to 3 this week, up 2300% from a 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69), indicating either a major construction project releasing hazardous material or newly-aware residents reporting exposure—critical for children's health in a dense residential area.
evidence: 3 construction lead dust complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
272 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (194 alterations) suggest ongoing renovation activity; lead dust typically emerges during pre-1978 building work
reporting_angles: Identify which specific construction projects are generating lead dust complaints; verify EPA/DOB lead abatement compliance.
Interview health department about testing and remediation protocols; speak with parents about child exposure risks and available testing.

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures in Multi-Family Housing
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints hit 36 two weeks ago, up 414% from a 7.0 weekly average (z-score: 7.03), suggesting widespread mechanical failures or deferred maintenance in Elmhurst's older multifamily housing stock—particularly serious for elderly and disabled residents.
evidence: 36 elevator complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 7.0 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 7.03 indicates statistically rare event
Community board has requested park and community facility upgrades repeatedly, suggesting infrastructure neglect as systemic issue
reporting_angles: Map elevator complaints to specific buildings; investigate landlord compliance with DOB inspection and maintenance requirements.
Interview disabled and elderly residents about how elevator outages affect mobility and access to medical care; request HPD enforcement action data.

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Disturbances Spike
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks jumped to 9 last week, up 800% from a 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 11.31), indicating either a new large event venue, unsupervised youth gatherings, or late-night commercial activity—conflicts with community board's repeated requests for park improvements.
evidence: 9 park noise complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Community board has requested park reconstruction/upgrades repeatedly, suggesting inadequate maintenance and enforcement infrastructure
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating noise complaints; speak with Parks Dept about event permits, programming, and enforcement hours.
Interview nearby residents and community board members about specific disturbances and what park improvements they're requesting.

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials & Mobile Vendors Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Both hazardous materials complaints (3 last week, +1100% from 0.2 avg) and mobile food vendor complaints (6 last week, +1100% from 0.5 avg) spiked simultaneously last week (both z-score: 6.35), suggesting either enforcement crackdowns revealing violations or new unregulated commercial activity posing health/environmental risks.
evidence: 3 hazardous materials complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (8-week baseline), z-score 6.35
6 mobile food vendor complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average, z-score 6.35
Parallel spike timing suggests possible coordinated inspections or seasonal shift in street-level commercial activity
reporting_angles: Query DSNY and DOHMH about enforcement operations last week; are these complaints from routine inspections or specific incident response?
Document unregulated mobile vendors and hazmat storage near schools, parks, or residential buildings; assess health code violations.
